question: For a four-leg intersection evaluated under the one-year Crash Experience signal warrant, what crash thresholds apply and what two additional categories of conditions must also be satisfied?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under the one-year Crash Experience warrant (Warrant 7), a four-leg intersection meets the crash-history condition if reported angle and pedestrian crashes in a 1-year period equal or exceed 5 (all severities) or 3 (fatal-and-injury) per Table 4C-2; where the major street exceeds 40 mph or the community has under 10,000 population, Table 4C-4 thresholds may be used instead (4 or 10 all-severity, and 3 or 6 fatal-and-injury, depending on the number of through lanes). In addition to the crash-history condition, two further criteria must also be met: (A) an adequate trial of alternatives has failed to reduce crash frequency, and (C) traffic volumes reach 80 percent of the Warrant 1 Condition A or Condition B values (or pedestrian volume reaches 80 percent of the Pedestrian Volume warrant) for each of any 8 hours of an average day. Guidance (recommended): - "The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that all of the following criteria are met: A. Adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce the crash frequency; and B. At least one of the following conditions applies to the reported crash history... 1. The number of reported angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total angle crashes and pedestrian crashes (all severities); or 2. The number of reported fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes... and C. For each of any 8 hours of an average day, the ve[hicles per hour given in both of the 80 percent columns of Condition A or Condition B in Table 4C-1 exist, or the pedestrian volume is not less than 80 percent of the Pedestrian Volume warrant requirements]." Options (permitted): - "If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on the major street exceeds 40 mph, or if the intersection lies within the built-up area of an isolated community having a population of less than 10,000: A. The traffic volumes in the 56 percent columns in Table 4C-1 may be used in place of the 80 percent columns. B. Tables 4C-4 and 4C-5 may be used in place of Tables 4C-2 and 4C-3, respectively." - Agencies may use documented agency-specific crash frequency values (from calibrated or agency-developed HSM safety performance functions) in place of the values in Tables 4C-2 through 4C-5. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 4C-2 shows that for four-leg intersections the one-year thresholds are 5 total angle and pedestrian crashes (all severities) and 3 fatal-and-injury angle and pedestrian crashes for all lane configurations. - [Image 2] Table 4C-4 (community less than 10,000 population or above 40 mph on the major street) shows four-leg one-year thresholds of 4 or 10 all-severity crashes and 3 or 6 fatal-and-injury crashes, depending on the number of through lanes on the major and minor streets. - [Image 3] Page 702 shows Section 4C.08 in full, including the Guidance criteria A, B, and C and Table 4C-2 with the four-leg thresholds of 5 and 3. Citations: - Section 4C.08 Guidance §2 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Option §5 (p.662) - Section 4C.08 Option §6 (p.663) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Support §7 (p.663) - Table 4C-2 (p.661) - Table 4C-4 (p.662) - Page 702
gold_answer: The thresholds are at least 5 all-severity angle/pedestrian crashes or at least 3 fatal-and-injury angle/pedestrian crashes. In addition, an adequate trial of alternatives must have failed, and the applicable 80-percent vehicular-volume or pedestrian-volume condition must be met for the required hours.
